name: ml-job-triage
description: Find which anomaly detection jobs are unhealthy and why: notification triage across all jobs, job/datafeed state, per-job messages, configuration, and what remediation was already tried. Use first for any ML job health question.
content:
# ML job triage

Start every ML job health question here.

1. `ml_notification_triage` (hours=24) - warning/error counts per job and kind: `delayed_data`, `no_data`, `extraction_error`, `no_node`, `memory`, `flush_error`.
2. `ad_get_jobs` - live job state (opened/closed/failed), datafeed state, memory status, `blocked.reason`.
3. `ad_get_job_messages` (job_id) - full message timeline for one job.
4. `ml_get_job_datafeed_config` - bucket_span, detectors, query_delay, indices, datafeed query.
5. `ml_remediation_history` (job_id or `*`) - what automation already did; never repeat a fix that failed in the last 24h.

## Classify, then load the matching skill
| Signal | Problem | Skill |
|---|---|---|
| job `failed`, "No node found to start datafeed", opened job with stopped datafeed | job/datafeed down | ml-job-recovery |
| "missed N documents due to ingest latency" | delayed data | ml-delayed-data |
| `memory_status` soft_limit/hard_limit, model snapshot reverts, `blocked.reason: revert` | memory / model state | ml-memory-and-model |
| "retrieving no data for a while" | source has no data - restart will not help | ml-job-recovery (preview the datafeed) |

"errors extracting data" on many jobs at the same time = one cluster-side incident (node restarts, search failures). Report it once.
Closed jobs are normally closed on purpose.
